proposal.hypothesis: Compared with the measured full-state cache (0.1790 s) and the x/y-cache hybrid without shared z state (0.2878 s), this variant tests whether a compact x/y smooth-weight-only cache plus shared per-octave z state can limit scratch traffic. It deliberately recomputes x/y lattice cells and fractions, so extra preprocessing may erase the saved weight work; no speedup is assumed.

retained: Add per-axis, per-octave smooth-weight arrays for x and y, using the original coordinate expression order before scaling by lambda.
Recompute x/y lattice cells and fractions for each pixel and octave instead of storing them; reuse precomputed z cell, offset, and smooth weight for each octave.

Retain the original gradient ordering, interpolation ordering, per-pixel accumulation, lambda progression, and amplitude progression; perform all allocations and state access within noise_serial timing.
